search_strategy: The agent cloned the repo, read the ticket-referenced source, then dumped every Mattermost channel to /tmp/chat/*.txt via the REST API (first attempt mis-escaped newlines into one giant line per channel, which it caught and re-dumped correctly). It ran broad OR-greps across all channels for 'capacity|per-minute|ratelimit|...' (step 42) and 'debt|refund|settlement|clamp' (step 52), each only showing head -50/-60 of much larger hit counts, then followed up with ~15 targeted `sed -n` reads of specific line ranges per channel once a thread looked live (pipeline, engineering, incidents, releases, cookbooks, general, viewer, code-review). It also grepped the wiki (search terms: debt/refund/settlement/capacity_budget/clamp, then x-ratelimit/anthropic-ratelimit/limit header/token_limit_strategy/seperate) and git history (git log -S for the same constants), finding nothing beyond the ticket. It never searched #help, #town-square, #off-topic, #random, or mail at all, and its #cookbooks/#pipeline/#code-review sweeps left several date ranges outside the windows it happened to sed — that is exactly where the 15 not-found clues (mostly the r1.s2 subtree and r2.s1/s2 leaves) live. Because each fact is carried redundantly by 3-6 remarks, missing roughly a third of the 46 remarks still left every fact with at least one surviving carrier, several of them (the debt-floor value, the refund/settle split, both counters) reinforced from 3+ independent remarks plus both reversals.
end_reason: Full pass. Merged to main (PR #737, merge commit 2c5bc96), CI green, deploy job completed — confirmed in the agent's own final summary and by the run's provenance.* = 1 fields in the pointer sheet.
notable: The two r1 herrings and both r2 herrings were all seen AND their reversals were all seen, in the same broad grep pass (step 42) that surfaced most of the corpus — the agent's Analysis at line 3578 explicitly flags 'the January design... was explicitly declared dead in April', so it never risked following a herring here.

g10.r1.g10.r1.s4.l1 carries both exclusions_or_crossover and observability and was actually seen twice: once garbled in the raw un-newlined dump (step 39, line 3275) and once cleanly in the capacity grep (step 42, line 3181) — the agent's Plan at line 3075 shows it noticed the garbled dump was informative before it even fixed the newline bug.

g10.r2.say25 (viewer.txt, 'available_request_capacity comes back as None... only the counters') was read very late (line 7987, well after capacity_budget.py was already fully written) and explicitly dismissed as a display-only question ('No settled display decision; leave display as-is', line 8025) — it happened to be redundant with the counters the agent had already built correctly from s5_l1-l4, so the miss cost nothing.

Every fact that passed did so with 3+ redundant remarks found, which is why the ~35% of remarks the agent never surfaced (mostly r1.s2 -per-axis-limit- subtree, and r2.s1/s2 leaves in #help/#cookbooks/#engineering date ranges the sed reads didn't reach) never touched the score.

The shipped `_refund_capacity(status_tracker, blocked_capacity)` call site (base_online_request_processor.py, patch7 at transcript line 5833) is placed BEFORE the `if request.attempts_left > 0:` branch, so one call site mechanically covers both the requeue and exhausted terminal paths — matching g10.r2.scope even though the requeue-specific leaf (s3_l4, 'charging the budget twice') was never found.
